verdict: OK to lend in Anantapur auto OEM-linked supply chain, but only to tier-1/tier-2 vendors with contracted volumes and clean receivables; avoid single-customer, low-margin job-work units.
title: Anantapur Cars & Commercial Vehicles (OEM): a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Anantapur is an assembly-and-supply cluster, not a market. Value sits with the OEM and its tier-1 tooling owners; the small vendor earns a conversion margin and carries the working capital.

Pricing power is thin: OEMs set piece prices and pass commodity inflation through with a lag. Peer evidence: Tata Motors CV volumes rose 26% but commodity inflation weighed on margins and prompted price increases [6]; M&M auto revenue grew 25% to ₹31,115 crore with EBIT margin at 9.5% [5]. **So when a proposal lands, check the price-escalation clause in the supply agreement; if there is none, ask how the last steel increase was absorbed.**

## What has changed now
National auto output is running hot: IIP NIC 29 output +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D]. **Bank credit to the sector is growing +27.0% YoY against +19.2% output — a +7.8 pp gap [D], meaning some of the growth is leverage, not demand.** Andhra Pradesh electricity demand is +18.1% Apr-to-date versus India's +9.5% [D], a genuine local activity signal. Locally, the Anantapur CII summit reported ₹4,141 crore of investment commitments [2]; commitments are not orders, so do not lend on the announcement. Peer commentary flags margin pressure from raw material and freight costs even as volumes stay strong [4][7].

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-1 and tier-2 vendors with two or more OEM customers, in-house tooling, and a purchase order book covering at least the loan tenor.** Avoid pure job-work units on a single customer and traders of imported parts. Structure as a cash-flow loan against assigned receivables with a 25% margin, monthly stock-and-debtor statements, and a covenant that total debt stays within a stated multiple of operating profit — rating methodology treats gearing and debt-to-operating-profit as core tests [10][11]. Take receivables ageing, order book and electricity bills every month.

- **Power consumption falls at the vendor's plant** — monthly; a sustained drop means lower output, so ask for dispatch records. - **Commodity price rise without a pass-through** — quarterly; if gross margin falls two quarters running, cut exposure.
